preflightNote: Storycraft Scale preflight runs on every attendant DeepSeek call (see server/mechanismTeaching.js).

113.title: Drowning
113.injuryMechanism: Ten-year-old jumped from a dock into shallow lake water — feet-first entry with axial load through the cervical spine at impact, then brief submersion with aspiration and hypoxia.
physicsBeats: Jump from height → kinetic energy converts to sudden deceleration when water surface arrests the body (water is nearly incompressible at impact — feels like hitting a wall, not a pillow).
Axial loading through the head/neck on a shallow or awkward entry can fracture or dislocate cervical vertebrae even without obvious external trauma.
Submersion after the impact → loss of airway protection → aspiration of water → surfactant washout and V/Q mismatch → hypoxemia and altered mental status.
Hypoxic brain injury and delayed pulmonary edema can evolve over hours — observation is not optional.

managementLinks.c-spine-precautions: Collar and inline stabilization limit secondary cord injury if an unstable C-spine fracture exists from the jump impact — you immobilize because the physics of the entry can break the spine before drowning steals the airway.
managementLinks.abcs-oxygen-airway: Hypoxia from submersion drives prognosis — restore oxygenation and protect the airway before surfactant injury and cerebral hypoxia compound.
managementLinks.cxr: Aspiration and surfactant loss produce infiltrates — the CXR shows the pulmonary consequence of the submersion phase.
managementLinks.abg: Quantifies hypoxemia and ventilation-perfusion mismatch after aspiration.
managementLinks.rewarming-if-hypothermic: Cold water drops core temperature — rewarming treats the thermodynamic stress that worsens perfusion and coagulation.
managementLinks.observation-all-victims: Delayed pulmonary edema can appear after a lucid interval — the mechanism continues in the lungs even when the child looks better.

113.teachingHook: Picture the jump: the water surface stops the body in milliseconds — that is when the neck can fail. Then the head goes under and the lungs take over the injury story.

176.title: Animal Bite
176.injuryMechanism: Young adult male — large dog bite to the right forearm about three hours before arrival. Crush-puncture contamination drives cellulitis and early sepsis: hypotension, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypoxemia, and elevated lactate — a whole-body inflammatory and sympathetic response, not an isolated skin wound.

patientAnchor.demographics: Young Black man, adult — subway-afro-dandy likeness; calm but clearly ill
patientAnchor.injurySite: Right forearm dog bite with surrounding cellulitis (NOT face/neck — do not default to facial airway compromise unless swelling threatens the upper airway)
patientAnchor.vitals: BP 82/50 · HR 116 · RR 24 · SpO₂ 87% room air · lactate 4.5

physicsBeats: Dog crush-puncture inoculates deep tissue with oral flora — pain and tissue injury trigger catecholamine surge (fear + pain + cytokines).
Tachypnea with SpO₂ 87%: he is moving air fast from sympathetic drive and early V/Q mismatch from sepsis — not necessarily primary lung disease.
BP 82/50 with HR 116 and lactate 4.5: perfusion is failing from systemic inflammatory response — fluids and source control matter as much as the local wound.
Forearm injury spares the airway structurally, but exhaustion and hypoxemia can still steal reserve while you irrigate and debride.

managementLinks.oxygen: His SpO₂ is 87% with RR 24 — supplemental O₂ widens reserve while catecholamine-driven tachypnea settles; you are buying margin before debridement and resuscitation, not treating a primary parenchymal lung disease.
managementLinks.stabilize: ABC first with these vitals: hypotensive and hypoxic — airway patent now but breathing is inefficient; circulation needs volume before cellulitis spreads.
managementLinks.stabilize-the-patient-ensure-airway-brea: Same as stabilize — anchor to BP 82/50 and SpO₂ 87%, not a generic trauma lecture.
managementLinks.iv-access: Two large-bore lines for fluid resuscitation — lactate 4.5 signals you need vascular access now.
managementLinks.iv-access-x2: Two large-bore lines for fluid resuscitation — lactate 4.5 signals you need vascular access now.
managementLinks.cbc: CBC and glucose with systemic illness — leukocytosis and stress hyperglycemia fit sepsis physiology in this presentation.
managementLinks.obtain-a-complete-blood-count-cbc-and-se: CBC and glucose with systemic illness — leukocytosis and stress hyperglycemia fit sepsis physiology in this presentation.
managementLinks.culture: Culture the wound after stabilization — forearm source drives bacteremia risk with this lactate.
managementLinks.culture-and-debridement-of-the-wound-if-: Irrigate and debride the forearm source after ABCs — cellulitis is the sepsis driver.
managementLinks.tetanus: Tetanus prophylaxis is wound-channel — separate beat from oxygen and fluids.
managementLinks.administer-tetanus-prophylaxis-if-needed: Tetanus prophylaxis is wound-channel — separate beat from oxygen and fluids.
managementLinks.rabies: ID consult for rabies PEP — dog bite timeline (~3h) matters; place after stabilization.
managementLinks.consult-infectious-disease-specialist-fo: ID for rabies immunoglobulin + vaccine series after ABCs and source control.

176.teachingHook: Look at the monitor first: 87% on room air with lactate 4.5 — the bite is on the forearm, but the body is already fighting systemically.
